turns.text_snippet: Let me look at how the memory system works and what triggers writes to it.
The Explore agent made a claim that memory capture isn't implemented, but I see merge commits that say otherwise. Let me verify the actual code.

Now I have a clear picture. The working directory is on `feature/git-workflow-skills`, but `main` has the full memory implementation.

**The direct answer to your question:** Creating a goal never writes to memory — not by design. Memory writes only happen when an agent run emits `MEMORY:` blocks in its output. The flow is:

```
agent stdout → memory_parser.py → MemoryStore.create(confirmed=False)
```

Goal creation has no path to the memory store. Only `worker._finalize()` (called after each agent run completes) triggers memory capture.

**Secondary issue — the working tree is stale:** The git repo at `/data/spaces/cronos-development` is checked out on `feature/git-workflow-skills`, not `main`. That branch is missing both `memory_parser.py` and `memory_retrieval.py`:

| Branch | `memory_parser.py` | `memory_retrieval.py` |
|--------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| `main` | ✅ present | ✅ present |
| `feature/git-workflow-skills` (HEAD) | ❌ missing | ❌ missing |

So if the app is running from the current working tree rather than `main`, the memory capture pipeline is entirely absent — agent runs won't capture `MEMORY:` blocks at all. The working tree needs to be switched to `main` (or the app needs to be rebuilt from `main`) for memory to work.
